profiles.shortDescription: Elco, trading as Regal Beloit Italy S.p.A., designs and manufactures electric motors and fans for refrigeration and air-conditioning equipment. Its range covers shaded-pole and electronically commutated (ECM) refrigeration motors, asynchronous and EC fan-coil motors, direct-driven centrifugal fans, fan decks, axial fans, gear motors, pre-mix combustion blowers and agitator motors. The products are supplied to OEMs building refrigerated cabinets and cells, fan coils, air-handling, condensing and evaporating units.
fullDescription: Elco's site states that the group's origins date back to 1954, when the Colombo family founded Elettromeccanica F.lli Colombo di Vittorio to manufacture electric motors for small electrical appliances in Italy. The first assembly plant abroad was established in Spain in 1982, followed by manufacturing plants in Brazil in 1998 and China in 2002. The group reports approximately 800 employees, about 160 of them at the Inzago plant between Bergamo and Milan, a site of roughly 40,000 m² that houses manufacturing together with top management, sales, administration and the R&D department. The company's footer identifies the legal entity as Regal Beloit Italy S.p.A., with its registered office in Milan and commercial and administrative offices at Ciserano (Zingonia, Bergamo).

The refrigeration range is described as the company's core business, aimed at OEMs in the refrigeration sector. It comprises shaded-pole motors from 2 W to 34 W for the commercial refrigeration market, ECM units built around a BLDC motor with integrated drivers, and a more compact ECM HC series that allows two separate speeds to be programmed wirelessly by RF, reversible speed or continuous 0-10 Vdc speed control. The site adds CF asynchronous compact axial fans and CFE EC axial fans from 300 mm to 400 mm with metal finger guards, states that products are VDE or UL/CSA approved and manufactured in Italy, China and Brazil, and dates the first Energy Saving (ECM) prototype to 1998. Typical applications named are refrigerated supermarket counters, refrigerated cells, ice cream and slush machines and small evaporating and condensing units.

For air treatment the site lists asynchronous motors from 12 W to 1.1 kW and EC motors from 12 W to 750 W, generally used in centrifugal fan blowers for fan coils or ducted air-conditioning units, plus direct-driven centrifugal fans in DD AC sizes 7/7 to 12/12 and DD EC sizes 9/7 to 12/12, and fan decks in the CO series and the energy-saving ECM CO series for fan coils and small air-handling units. Stated HVAC applications include condensing units, fan coils, air curtains, extractor hoods, heat recovery and air-handling units. A further group of products covers custom gear motors for slush machines and cold drink dispensers, cast-aluminium pre-mix combustion blowers for domestic and industrial boiler units, and enclosed IP65 agitator motors for the beverage dispensing industry.

profiles.shortDescription: MIL'S manufactures vacuum pumps, vacuum systems, compressed-air plants and oxygen generators. Its healthcare range supplies hospitals with centralised medical air, technical air, oxygen and vacuum installations, while its industrial range covers lubricated, oil-less and water vacuum pumps and systems. The company states it was founded in 1926 and is based in Genas near Lyon, France.
fullDescription: The site presents MIL'S as a manufacturer specialising in the health sector, with equipment designed to supply hospital establishments and medical facilities through centralised gas distribution networks. Its healthcare offering is split into Air (medical air plants and technical air plants), Oxygen (PSA and VPSA oxygen generators, oxygen filling stations, cabins and containers) and Vacuum (vacuum pumps, vacuum systems, laboratory and anaesthetic-gas vacuum systems, emergency cabinets).

Medical air plants are marketed under the HOSPITAIR name, with the site listing HOSPITAIR 1/2, HOSPITAIR C, HOSPITAIR G, HOSPITAIR PACK, HOSPITAIR SKID, HOSPITAIR HYPERBARE and the oil-free HOSPITAIR SCROLAIR 1/2, SCROLAIR G, SCROLAIR PACK and SCROLAIR PACK D versions. Technical air, used inside hospitals for laundry, pneumatic doors and sterilisers, is covered by oilless piston compressors and the AIRMIL'S 1/2 and AIRMIL'S G ranges in 7, 10 and 15 bar piston or 8, 11 and 15 bar screw versions.

For industry, the site groups the offering into lubricated vacuum pumps, oil-less vacuum pumps, water vacuum pumps and vacuum systems, and notes that the company has used the piston compressor as a vacuum pump since 1926. It describes itself as a French family SME with more than 100 employees, two production sites totalling 12,500 m², an R&D department for customer-specific adaptations, and ISO 9001, ISO 13485 and ISO 14001 certification, with installations complying with ISO 7396-1 for medical gas systems.

profiles.shortDescription: NiMCO Corporation builds form, fill and seal machines for gable-top cartons. Its range runs from hand and semi-automatic sealers to automatic and custom machines filling containers from 120 ml to 5 litres, with spout-applicator and hydrogen-peroxide sterilisation options. The company states it was established in 1962 and is based in Crystal Lake, Illinois.
fullDescription: The site describes NiMCO as an independent manufacturer of form, fill and seal equipment for gable-top cartons, with over 2000 installations in more than 60 countries. Machines are grouped as Hand Machines, Semi-Automatic Machines, Automatic Machines and Custom Machines, with a separate Cross Cartons line and a parts and service offering.

The product line is organised by container size: Mini, Quart/Liter, 1/2 Gallon/2 Liter, Gallon/4 Liter and Special. The quart/litre pages print the 180QL, 280QL, 380QL, 580QL, 680QL, 8085QL and 8300QL models, and the gallon pages the 180G, 210G, 655G, 755G and 780G models.

Two options recur across the range: the CAP-PAC Spout Applicator and the Ultra Clean H2O2 sterilisation package, offered on the higher-output models. The applications sections divide end uses into food products and non-food products, naming beverage and juice, deli and salad, snack and cookie, and personal care users.

profiles.shortDescription: Cometal Engineering S.p.A. designs and manufactures machinery and complete production lines for aluminium extrusion and foundry plants. Its equipment includes melting and holding furnaces, billet casting and homogenising lines, extrusion presses, handling, aging and packing lines. The company is based in Montichiari, in the province of Brescia, Italy.
fullDescription: Cometal Engineering was founded in 1980 and has its headquarters in Montichiari, Brescia, Italy. The company states that it designs and produces complete extrusion lines including presses, foundries, heat treatment solutions and packing lines, and that it also supplies individual machines and upgrades to existing plants. Production is carried out in Italy using Italian and Western European components.

The foundry range published on the site covers Single Chamber Melting Furnaces, Twin Chamber Melting Furnaces, Holding Furnaces, the Billets Casting Line, the Logs Homogenizing Centre and the Logs Automatic Stacker, addressing the melting, holding, casting and homogenising stages of aluminium billet production.

The extrusion range listed on the site runs from the Logs/Billets Feeding Line, Logs/Billets Heating, Logs Cutting and Press Billet Loading through Extrusion Presses, Cooling Systems at Press Exit, Pullers & Saws, Die Heating Oven, Extrusion Table, Stretcher, Cut to Length Systems and Scrap Cutting Machine, to the Stacking/De-stacking System, Aging Line, Baskets/Layers Handling and Packing line. The company states it operates internationally through subsidiaries in Texas, United States, established in 2015, and in Foshan, China, established in 2004, which provide equipment, technical support, spare parts and training.

profiles.shortDescription: EMP s.r.o. is a Czech manufacturer of asynchronous electric motors and electric pumps based in Slavkov u Brna. Its catalogue covers single-phase, three-phase and built-in motors, submersible motors in IP68, and immersible, high-pressure, multistage and gear pumps. The company states that it supplies tailor-made electric motors to industrial customers.
fullDescription: EMP s.r.o. states that it was established in 1991, took over from MEZ Brno during the privatisation process and resumed manufacturing on 1 July 1994 at Nádražní 394, Slavkov u Brna. The site describes computerised motor design facilities and factory logistics, CNC machinery and automated testing equipment, and lists ISO 9001, ISO 14001 and Blue Competence certifications.

The product directory is divided into Asynchronous Electric Motors, Electric Pumps and Special Submersible Motors. Single-phase motors are listed as the JMC series with permanent capacitor and the JME capacitor start–capacitor run series, each also offered in versions compliant with the IE1 efficiency class; three-phase motors comprise the TM series up to 0.75 kW, the TM2 series in IE2, the TM3 series in IE3 and pole-changing motors, with built-in single-phase and three-phase variants and JMZ and TMZ motors in IP68.

The pump range is catalogued by series with head and flow data: COA and COP immersible pumps, COV high-pressure pumps, COS and COSM multistage pumps and CZ gear pumps. The company states that it produces more than 200 types of electric motors and pumps per annum.

profiles.shortDescription: TECNOMEC 3 SRL designs and builds spreader rolls and related web-handling components at its site in Turbigo, Italy. Its range covers rubber-covered spreader roll series for paper, textile, plastic and converting machines, rubber spiral rolls, Teflon (FEP and PFA) covers and mounting brackets. The company also refurbishes spreader rolls of other makes.
fullDescription: The company page states that TECNOMEC 3 has worked in this field for 35 years and that its activity is based on planning and building spreader rolls and special products for different fields. It describes technical assistance before and after the sale, agents worldwide, and production capacity both for new rolls and for refurbishment carried out for any brand. The site footer gives the address Via Cascinaccia Bassa, 1/D, 20029 Turbigo (MI), Italy.

The product section is organised by application - Paper Industry, Textile Industry, Plastic Industry and Converting - with a distinct roll series for each. Series A is described for extruded, calendered, coated and multilayer plastic films, dry fabrics, paper and cardboard, aluminium and felts, in sizes A75 to A200. Series B is described for fabrics and felts in cool or warm, dry or wet applications, in sizes B85 to B175. Series G is a rubber spreader roll listed for tissue machines, size press, coating machines, press section, pope and cutter, in sizes G125 to G350. The pages also list variants with variable bow, with axle cooled, with lubrication, with elastic bands, with steel stave, a paper guide execution and a Series M.

Separate product pages cover the accessory ranges. Brackets are offered as Series FB, Series FF and Series RM, together with rotating brackets Series RU in sizes RU30 to RU210 plus an RU75/P variant and matching bases B30 to B210. The Teflon cover page describes thermo-shrinking pipes of fluorocarbonic resins in FEP and PFA, used for spreader rolls and for other rolls in steel, alloys or rubber. Rubber spiral rolls are described as needing no control or inner supports, with a reusable inner shaft available in aluminium, steel or carbon.

profiles.shortDescription: Bühler Motor GmbH develops and manufactures electric drive technology: DC and BLDC motors, gear motors, actuators, electric pumps and encoders/brakes. The company supplies customer-specific drive solutions to the automotive, healthcare, industrial and aviation sectors, and also offers standard motors and gear motors from a stock delivery programme. It is a family-owned company headquartered in Nuremberg, Germany.
fullDescription: The history page traces the company to 1855, when brothers Adolf and Karl Heinrich Bühler founded a clock factory in Triberg in the Black Forest. It was acquired by Josef Furtwängler in 1892 and renamed Gebrüder Bühler Nachfolger; production moved to Nuremberg in 1925, which remains the headquarters. The first electric motor followed in 1955, the first North American production plant in 1974, own production in China in 1998, the first product with integrated electronics in 2009, and the acquisition of Dornier Technologie Systems in 2017, which established the aviation division. The legal notice names Bühler Motor GmbH, Anne-Frank-Str. 33-35, 90459 Nuremberg, registered at the Nuremberg court under HRB 258.

The site is organised into four markets, each with its own product pages. Industrial products are listed as motors (DC and BLDC motors for customer-specific applications or from the instant delivery programme), gear motors (planetary, spur and worm gears combined with DC and BLDC motors) and encoders/brakes (optical and magnetic encoders and brakes for motion control). Automotive products are listed as motors and actuators and electric pumps, with applications in drivetrain, thermal and emissions systems and e-mobility. Healthcare products cover motors, gear motors, micro-drives and encoders/brakes for drug delivery devices and medical equipment, while aviation covers seat actuation, control panels, pneumatic systems and customised components. Industrial applications named on the site include building automation, agriculture, transportation and office equipment.

The facts and figures page states approximately 1,050 staff worldwide, more than 200 development engineers, around 17 million units produced each year, approximately 25 distribution partners and eight business sites on three continents, with the company describing itself as family-owned and self-financed. The stock service programme lists standard drives by frame size with their type numbers, including DC Motor 24 flat (1.16.011.5XX), DC Motor 22 x 48 (1.13.078.0XX), DC Motor 31 x 42 (1.13.021.7XX), DC Motor 31 x 51 (1.13.021.3XX) and DC Motor 31 x 75 (1.13.021.6XX), alongside EC motor and gear motor ranges.

profiles.shortDescription: KELLER Pressure AG manufactures piezoresistive pressure measurement products in Winterthur, Switzerland. Its range covers OEM pressure transducers, pressure transmitters, submersible level probes, data loggers, digital pressure gauges, wireless transmission units and custom solutions. The products are supplied to vehicle, aviation, oil and gas, water and environment, HVAC and process-industry users.
fullDescription: The company page states that KELLER Pressure was founded in 1974 by Hannes W. Keller, the inventor of the integrated silicon measuring cell, and that his sons Tobias and Michael Keller are now responsible for the business. The company is described as wholly family-owned, employing around 500 people from over 20 nations, with fourteen branches in Europe, Asia and the USA supported by representatives and distributors elsewhere. Value creation and most employment are stated to be at the Winterthur headquarters, and the company is certified to ISO 9001. The legal notice gives the entity as KELLER Pressure AG, St. Gallerstrasse 122, 8404 Winterthur, Switzerland.

The product catalogue is divided into eight sections: pressure transducers, pressure transmitters, level probes, data loggers, digital pressure gauges, wireless solutions, custom solutions and software and accessories. Transducers include OEM types Series 3L, 4L, 7L, 9L and 10L, miniature types Series M5 and 2MI without oil filling, high-pressure types Series 6LHP, 7LHP and 10LHP, and differential types Series PD-10L and PD-10LHP. Transmitters cover standard Series 21Y, 21C, 21PY, 23SX, 23SY, 33X and 41X, analog Series 23 and 25, and differential Series PD-23X, PD-33X and PD-39X. Level probes include Series 26X, 26KYX, 26Y, 36XS, 36XW, 36XiW and 46X, plus multi-parameter Series 36XW CTD and 36XiW CTD.

Data loggers are published as level loggers DCX-16, DCX-22, DCX-22 ECO, DCX-22AA and DCX-25PVDF, multi-parameter loggers DCX-22 CTD and DCX-22AA CTD, and pressure loggers LEO-Record and LEO5; the DCX-22 page describes measurement of water level, pressure and temperature with a battery life of up to ten years at one measurement per hour, in sealed gauge, vented gauge and cable-free versions, supported by PressureSuite Desktop software and the K-114 converter. Digital pressure gauges are listed as LEO1, LEO2, LEO3, LEO5, LEO-Record, LEO-Ultimate, LEX1 and ECO2. For hazardous areas the site publishes intrinsically safe Ei variants such as Series 36XW Ei, Series 46X Ei, LEO1 Ei and ECO2 Ei, and flameproof Ed variants such as Series 23 Ed, 25 Ed, 33X Ed and 35X Ed. Wireless remote transmission units are listed as ADT1 and ARC1 in box and tube versions. The industry pages cover vehicles, aviation and spaceflight, oil and gas, water and environment, HVAC, raw material extraction, chemistry, food and pharma, consumer products, structural measuring, and system and device construction.

profiles.shortDescription: Kovalus Separation Solutions, LLC, formerly Koch Membrane Systems and Koch Separation Solutions, manufactures membrane filtration elements and separation process equipment. Its portfolio covers spiral, hollow fiber, tubular and ceramic membranes for microfiltration, ultrafiltration, nanofiltration and reverse osmosis, together with ion exchange, evaporation and drying, powder packaging and cheese processing systems. Customers are in dairy, food and beverage, life sciences, general industry and municipal and industrial water treatment.
fullDescription: The company's history and brands page records that the business began in 1963 as Abcor, Inc., formed to develop and commercialise processes and equipment based on separation and purification technologies. Koch Engineering Company acquired it in 1977 and the business was renamed Koch Membrane Systems, Inc. in 1981, then Koch Separation Solutions in 2020. In September 2023 Sun Capital Partners purchased the business from Koch Engineered Solutions and it was rebranded Kovalus Separation Solutions. The same page lists the acquisitions that built the portfolio: Romicon, Inc. in 1991, MPW in 1996, Fluid Systems Corporation in 1998, Puron AG in 2004, Eco-Tec, Inc. in 2019 and RELCO in November 2020. The locations page gives the corporate headquarters and manufacturing site as 850 Main Street, Wilmington, Massachusetts, USA.

The membrane filtration section groups the products by membrane geometry. Spiral products are FLUID SYSTEMS® Elements, KPAK® PLUS Potted Spiral, EDCORE® Electrodialysis Cell, Sani-Pro® Elements and SelRO®. Hollow fiber products are ASPIDA™ Modules, PURON® MBR and PULSION® MBR Modules, PURON® HF and PURON® MP Modules, ROMICON® and ROMIPRO™ Cartridges, and WINEFILTER™ and BEERFILTER™. Tubular products are SUPER-COR® and SUPER-G™ Modules and FEG PLUS® Modules, and there is a KSS Ceramic Membranes line. The FLUID SYSTEMS element page documents the TFC® types, with TFC SR for nanofiltration, TFC HR, FR and ULP for brackish water reverse osmosis and TFC SW and HF for seawater reverse osmosis, supplied as elements or in pre-engineered packaged and modular RO/NF systems.

Beyond membranes, the technologies section lists ion exchange based on the Recoflo reciprocating flow process, cleaning solutions, the SepTrac™ smart system for monitoring and optimising performance, evaporation and drying equipment under the RELCO brand, powder and packaging handling systems, and cheese technology. Applications named for the membrane systems include industrial and municipal water and wastewater, wastewater treatment for reuse, polishing of UF or MF permeate, production of high purity deionised water, brackish water treatment and seawater desalination. The markets pages cover dairy, food, beverage, life sciences, general industrial, oil and gas, mining and metals refining, textile, pulp and paper, automotive, water and wastewater, and lithium processing.

profiles.shortDescription: BackTech SAM GmbH develops and builds machines and lines for dough processing, principally dough dividing and rounding machines together with forming, docking and proofing systems. It supplies bakeries worldwide, from craft bakers to industrial production. The company states it specialises in the whole range of small baked goods, lye pastry, pretzels and pizza.
fullDescription: BackTech SAM's company page states that the business was created in 2016 through the merger of Back-Tech Austria and SAM Bäckereitechnik, that it brings together more than 25 years of experience and worldwide references, and that its seat is today in Hallbergmoos near Munich Airport. The imprint gives the legal entity as BackTech SAM GmbH, Zengerstr. 25, 85399 Hallbergmoos, registered in the Munich commercial register.

The site presents the range under German category names: dough dividing and rounding machines, compact systems, shaped-pastry lines, element systems, compact dough-belt lines, multifunctional systems, industrial plant and the BREWIC / WiBrez group, with a further section for used equipment. Named machines include Bavaria Evolution and Mega-Star dividers, the Roll-Maker and Remi-Line compact systems, CompactLine M and COMPACTLINE DUO K/L/S, the COMFORTLINE, Multi-Star and PREMIUMLINE element lines, SquareLine, CAROLINE and the Robo-Star automatic tray-loading system.

The company describes its element systems as precisely matched and freely combinable, states that PREMIUMLINE reaches up to 9,000 pieces per hour with single-operator control, and says customer requirements for dough processing and transport are covered either by its own developments or by products from cooperation partners. Industrial plant is offered under the BackTech SAM Grubelnik name.

profiles.shortDescription: UniMac is the commercial and on-premises laundry equipment brand of Alliance Laundry Systems, LLC. Its documented range covers washer-extractors, tumble dryers, stacked washer-extractor/tumble dryer combinations, light commercial machines and firefighter PPE drying cabinets. The equipment is supplied to on-premises laundry operations rather than to consumers.
fullDescription: UniMac's own product directory organises the range into washer-extractors, tumble dryers, stacked washer-extractor/tumble dryers, light commercial equipment and a PPE drying cabinet. The washer-extractor line is published in hardmount and softmount configurations, spanning high-performance and mid-performance UW Series hardmount machines, cabinet hardmount and value-line cabinet models, and softmount units, with capacities stated from 20 lb up to 275 lb depending on the line. A dedicated UM202 top-load washer-extractor is described for car wash environments with stainless steel construction, two wash tubs and a centre extractor.

The site addresses on-premises laundry operators and lists the segments it serves as hospitality, fire departments, healthcare and long-term care, athletics, corrections, spa and salon, maritime, dry cleaners, restaurants, commercial laundry and dairy. Product pages describe the equipment in terms of controls, extraction G-force and total cost of ownership, and reference the brand's own OPTispray, OPTidry and ProCapture technologies.

Contact details published on unimac.com give Alliance Laundry Systems, LLC at 221 Shepard Street, Ripon, Wisconsin, United States, and the site links to Alliance Laundry parts and dealer portals, identifying UniMac as a brand operated within that company.

profiles.shortDescription: Rotex Group manufactures industrial screeners, separators, sifters and grain cleaners, together with particle-size analyzers, feeders and conveyors. Its machines use gyratory, gyratory-reciprocating and vibratory motion for dry separation of bulk materials. The company operates as part of the Advanced Process Solutions Group owned by Hillenbrand, Inc.
fullDescription: Rotex Group states that it has led in industrial separations, sifting and grain cleaning innovations since 1844, and identifies itself as part of the Advanced Process Solutions Group owned by Hillenbrand, Inc. (NYSE: HI). Its headquarters is published as 1230 Knowlton St., Cincinnati, Ohio, with further locations listed in Runcorn in the United Kingdom, Chiba in Japan, Wuxi in China, Chembur in India and a sales office in Gernsbach, Germany.

The product catalogue covers screeners and separators including the Rotex gyratory reciprocating screener, Apex, Ultrex, the Minerals Separator and Megatex XD, Classic Screen and Chip Screen, Super Screen and CounterFlow Super Screen, the CounterFlow CS Model, RTX360, Multi-Deck and Super-Deck screens, Hi Cline, the Megatex Grain Cleaner, the Chip Classifier and Plastic Pellet Screener, plus Gradex 2000 particle-size analyzers, the Chip Feeder and the Direct Drive Feeder.

The Rotex screener page describes a patented gyratory reciprocating motion that starts as purely gyratory at the head, becomes elliptical in the centre and reverts to reciprocating toward the discharge end, and lists general purpose and dairy screener variants. Applications published by the company cover agriculture, chemical, fertilizer, food, forest products, minerals, plastics, recycling and miscellaneous industrial processing.

profiles.shortDescription: ALLTEC Angewandte Laserlicht Technologie GmbH manufactures laser marking and engraving systems under the FOBA brand. Its range covers marking lasers in fiber, CO2, UV, green and ultrashort-pulse technologies, laser marking machines, marking software, vision systems and automation packages. The systems are supplied for direct part marking and traceability in industrial production.
fullDescription: The imprint identifies the operating company as ALLTEC Angewandte Laserlicht Technologie GmbH, An der Trave 27-31 in Selmsdorf, Germany, registered at the Schwerin district court under HRB 7884, and states that it trades under the FOBA Laser Marking + Engraving brand.

The product portfolio is organised into laser marking systems - ultrashort pulse, CO2, fiber, UV and green laser markers - plus laser marking machines, laser marking software, vision systems, and automation and process integration. The M-Series marking machines are described as turnkey and custom laser processing machines for stand-alone operation in laser class 1, configurable with different lasers, powers, axis systems and loading concepts; options include rotary tables and camera systems.

The site lists automotive, medical technology, mechanical engineering, plastic processing, electronics and semiconductors, and tool, metal and mold marking as the industries served, and names metals, plastics, ceramics, lacquers, glass and organic materials as markable substrates. Marking processes described include laser marking, annealing, colour change and foaming, carbonization, colour or material removal, and laser engraving.

profiles.shortDescription: FIBRO Rundtische GmbH manufactures rotary tables for machine tools and automation systems. The range is divided into automation rotary tables and machining rotary tables, and the company states that it offers more than 150 rotary table types together with accessories. The tables are used as swivel axes, in machining applications and in assembly and transfer tasks.
fullDescription: The company gives its founding year as 1958 in Weinsberg, states that it was part of the LÄPPLE Group from 1974, and that it has operated as an independent company since 2024. Its headquarters remain in Weinsberg, Germany, with subsidiaries in the USA, India and China.

The product directory groups the range into two families. Under automation the site lists FIBROTOR ER, FIBROTOR EM, FIBROTOR EM.NC, FIBROTOR VR.NC and FIBROMAT AT; under machining it lists FIBROPLAN, FIBRODYN DA, FIBROTAKT and FIBROMAX. Alongside the standard programme the company offers bespoke solutions adapted to specific process requirements.

The site describes rotary tables for automation systems and machine tools as usable in a variety of ways, whether as swivel axes or in assembly tasks, and names powertrain and automotive production, aerospace, medical technology and semiconductor manufacturing among the fields in which its tables are applied.

profiles.shortDescription: UDICOM Elettronica designs and builds electronic equipment for industrial plants. Its catalogue covers fanless industrial PCs and panel PCs, LCD panel and keyboard units, CAN bus and axis-control modules, signal-interface converters, GPS timing and solar-tracking units, and measuring instruments. The company also offers restoration and repair of older electronic devices.
fullDescription: UDICOM presents itself as a designer and builder of electronic equipment for industrial plants, operating from Via Cotonificio 47 in Tavagnacco, in the province of Udine, Italy. Its product directory is organised around industrial computing, communication and interface hardware rather than around a single machine type.

The documented range includes the Kaparossa fanless industrial PC, panel PCs and an 8.4" touch PC, LCD panel and keyboard assemblies in 8", 12.1" and 17" formats, CAN modules and a CAN axis control module, a 5-channel infrared receiver, an encoder signal converter for LineDriver/PushPull signals, the SynchroMaster, the GPS Synchro Timer Cricket, the SunTracker solar tracker and the MultiMetro instrument. Several system products are listed under KS designations.

Alongside new equipment, the site states that UDICOM carries out electronic restoration work, repairing and refurbishing devices produced decades earlier, which positions the company as a supplier both of current automation hardware and of support for installed legacy electronics.

profiles.shortDescription: Steelbau manufactures stainless steel bowls and hoppers for industrial mixers. Its range covers deep pressed drawn bowls for spiral, fork and twin-arm mixers, planetary bowls, tailor-made and special bowls, hoppers and mixing tools. The products are supplied for food, chemical-pharmaceutical and cosmetic applications.
fullDescription: Steelbau states that it was founded in 1990 in Schio, in the province of Vicenza, as a specialist in the transformation of stainless steel for the food industry. The company reports a merger with Inox Fondi in 2020 and the opening of a new production facility in Isola Vicentina in 2021, where it is now located at Via Bacchiglione 36.

The product range consists of stainless steel bowls in various capacities — standard, special and tailor-made — together with hoppers and accessories. Deep pressed drawn bowls are offered in versions for spiral mixers, fork mixers and twin arms mixers, alongside planetary bowls; the accessories listed are the spiral hook, fork tool, cutting blade and whip. The site presents these as components made without welding using the company's own drawing technology.

Applications named by the manufacturer cover bread making, confectionery, dairy and meat processing, with the same bowl and hopper technology extended to chemical-pharmaceutical and cosmetic production. The company describes annual output in the thousands of units and export sales to more than thirty countries.
